skill.name: cc-pr-review-ci
skill.description: Comprehensive TypeScript/React PR review. Outputs structured review.json consumed by a posting script that creates a GitHub Review with inline comments. Agent runs read-only; the workflow script holds write permissions.
skill.summary: Review TypeScript and React changes across twelve domains, then prepare structured findings for a separate GitHub posting step.
skill.author: adrianbrowning

security_audit.summary: Most static flags identify Markdown, JavaScript strings, legitimate credential use, or ordinary repository review operations. Confirmed risks include unvalidated shell interpolation and predictable temporary review input. Semantic findings identify unauthenticated finding suppression, marker-based dismissal of other reviewers, and approval binding to a potentially unreviewed head commit.

remediation.issue: Repository and PR environment values enter shell commands without validation.
remediation.suggestion: Use execFileSync with argument arrays; validate repository identifiers and require a positive integer PR number before invoking GitHub CLI.

remediation.issue: The default review artifact uses a predictable shared temporary path.
remediation.suggestion: Use a private per-job directory and explicit artifact path; reject symlinks, verify ownership, and validate the review schema before posting.

remediation.issue: Any negative reaction or dismissal phrase can silently suppress a finding.
remediation.suggestion: Accept dismissals only from authorized maintainers, record their identities, and include suppressed findings in an auditable review section.

remediation.issue: A body marker alone identifies reviews eligible for dismissal.
remediation.suggestion: Verify the expected bot identity and REQUEST_CHANGES state; create the replacement successfully before dismissing only that bot's prior review.

remediation.issue: The posting script fetches the latest head instead of verifying the reviewed commit.
remediation.suggestion: Include the analyzed head SHA in the review artifact and reject posting when the current PR head differs.

semantic_findings.title: Unauthenticated Dismissals Suppress Security Findings
semantic_findings.description: Any negative reaction or human reply containing dismissal language qualifies without an authorization check. Matching findings are then skipped silently, allowing participants to hide unresolved issues.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Fetched replies omit author identity, and reactions are treated as counts. The explicit suppression rule cannot distinguish maintainer decisions from other participants.

semantic_findings.title: Spoofable Marker Permits Dismissal of Other Reviewers
semantic_findings.description: Existing reviews are selected only by a body marker, without checking author identity. The script attempts dismissal before successfully posting a replacement, potentially removing legitimate blocking reviews.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The query selects review IDs solely by body text, and the retrieved state is ignored. Impact depends on the token having review dismissal permission.

semantic_findings.title: Approval Can Target an Unreviewed Head Commit
semantic_findings.description: The script fetches the current PR head and attaches the earlier review artifact to that commit. A push between analysis and posting can receive approval without being reviewed.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The loaded artifact is not compared with an analyzed commit SHA. The API payload uses only the head fetched during posting.

content.user_title: Review TypeScript and React Pull Requests
content.value_statement: Pull request reviews can miss issues across security, tests, performance, and maintenance. This skill organizes twelve review domains and prepares findings for GitHub comments.
actual_capabilities: Read a GitHub pull request diff and metadata, or compare local changes against origin/main.
Guide sequential reviews across twelve domains, including security, React, TypeScript, testing, CI, and maintainability.
Prepare structured findings with stable identifiers, paths, optional line numbers, explanations, fixes, and suggested repair prompts.
Use a separate Node.js script to post a GitHub review with inline or file-level comments and severity counts.
Suppress previously dismissed findings and reconsider them when nearby code changes or comparison fails.
Review an existing jscpd duplication report when available and skip that domain when the report is absent.
limitations: Findings rely on AI analysis; this workflow does not prove correctness or replace human review.
Test validity requires a separately installed skill, and duplication review requires an existing jscpd report.
The package does not include a CI workflow that enforces permission separation; reference paths assume a Claude-style installation.
The posting script needs shell, artifact, dismissal, and commit validation hardening before use in shared or untrusted CI environments.

use_cases.title: Check Changes Before Opening a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Review local TypeScript and React changes against origin/main and inspect the structured results before requesting team feedback.

use_cases.title: Prepare Consistent Repository Reviews
use_cases.description: Use domain checklists to prepare actionable findings with stable identifiers and proposed fixes for human assessment.

use_cases.title: Integrate Review Artifacts into CI
use_cases.description: Separate AI review generation from credentialed posting after hardening the script and configuring permissions in an external workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Review Local Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current changes against origin/main using cc-pr-review-ci. Print the structured review locally and do not post comments.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: inspect changes without a PR number.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Review PR [number] across all twelve domains. Prepare the review artifact, report skipped domains, and leave GitHub posting to the separate script.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: prepare findings for an existing PR.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Tests and CI
prompt_templates.prompt: Review PR [number] across all domains, emphasizing test validity and CI permissions. State missing dependencies and explain each proposed fix.
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced: assess testing and workflow changes.

prompt_templates.title: Reassess a Changed Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Re-review PR [number] after recent commits. Verify authorized dismissals, reassess changed finding locations, and report suppressions for human approval before posting.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: apply explicit oversight to repeat reviews.

output_examples.input: Review local changes that add tests with mocks returning the asserted values.
output: High priority: A test asserts its mock output without exercising production behavior.
Suggested fix: Execute the production path and assert observable results.
Review decision: Approved with suggestions unless a critical issue is also found.

output_examples.input: Review a workflow supporting both pull requests and manual runs.
output: High priority: Pull request fields are used during manual runs, where those fields are unavailable.
Suggested fix: Select valid metadata for each supported event.
The review artifact includes a finding identifier, location, explanation, and repair prompt.

best_practices: Harden and validate the posting script, bind artifacts to reviewed commits, and use private per-job artifact storage.
Keep AI review credentials read-only and grant the separate posting step only the GitHub permissions it requires.
Review findings and suppressions manually, and provide optional testing skills and duplication reports when those domains matter.
anti_patterns: Run the current posting script with untrusted environment values or a broadly privileged token.
Treat missing optional domains or AI approval as evidence that tests passed or security is guaranteed.
Accept arbitrary reactions as authorized dismissals or post an old review after the PR head changes.

faq.question: What languages and frameworks does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets TypeScript and React pull requests, with additional checklists for security, testing, CI, scope, documentation comments, and maintainability.

faq.question: Can I use it without a pull request?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares changes against origin/main and prints the structured review to standard output.

faq.question: Does the reviewing agent publish comments?
faq.answer: The instructions prohibit direct posting. A separate Node.js script uses GitHub CLI to publish the review; an external workflow must enforce permissions.

faq.question: Does it execute tests or generate duplication reports?
faq.answer: Test validity review is static. Duplication review consumes an existing jscpd report rather than generating one.

faq.question: Which optional skills are needed?
faq.answer: Test validity requires test-validity-review. Testing can use testing-best-practice, but retains a built-in checklist when that skill is unavailable.

faq.question: Is the posting script ready for untrusted CI inputs?
faq.answer: No. Add shell-free execution, artifact validation, authorized dismissal checks, and reviewed-commit verification before using it with untrusted inputs.
